title: Improve software-rendered Surface depth with the installed ProceduralTerrains visual profile

scope.subject: Improve the AUTO/software Surface fallback's visible relief, tonal separation and distance depth using only the installed ProceduralTerrains terrain configuration and existing hosted visual acceptance, without adding clouds, water, a second renderer, extra scene passes or another camera authority

research_summary: Hosted mobile Surface evidence is now world-correct but visually flat: the Infinite World boundary is gone, yet the low-octave SwiftShader profile reads as a pale ground sheet with weak near/mid/far separation. ProceduralTerrains 2.0.5 already exposes terrain-owned palette saturation/contrast/tint, sun intensity/color, sky ambient, ground bounce, sun elevation, fog density and height scale as configuration/uniform controls. Its runtime README also states that terrain shaders own their sun/ambient lighting rather than adopting arbitrary host-scene lights. The lowest-cost product fix is therefore a software-only terrain visual profile that keeps the existing seed, two-octave shader, streaming/LOD budgets and renderer lifecycle unchanged, while the existing Playwright narrow Surface cases provide promotion evidence. Optional water/cloud effects are deliberately rejected on the software path because they add effect work to the exact renderer tier being protected.

sources.finding: ProceduralTerrains 2.0.5 is the installed MIT runtime release; its world runtime and performance controls are already the supported surface subsystem rather than a product-owned terrain replacement.

The caller-owned runtime exposes terrain configuration for style/lighting and documents that its built-in terrain shaders use their own sun/ambient lighting; water and clouds are explicit optional layers rather than required terrain features.
The existing Playwright release suite can capture the same mobile/tablet Surface viewports after tuning, preserving comparable hosted visual evidence without another screenshot framework.

Three.js scene fog is a generic host-scene mechanism, but the current terrain uses its own shader fog uniform; adding a separate product fog mechanism would duplicate a capability already exposed by ProceduralTerrains.

search_ladder.conclusion: No full terrain/sky product should replace the existing Surface subsystem for a tonal-depth defect; the installed runtime already owns the terrain and exposes the required visual controls.
Keep the existing R3F host and Playwright acceptance. Generic scene fog/lights are not promoted as a second visual authority because the terrain shader already owns equivalent controls.
Reuse ProceduralTerrains' existing style, lighting, palette and height configuration to tune only the software fallback while retaining its current Infinite World, lifecycle and performance budgets.
No new model, sprite, sky dome, fog mesh or decorative asset is needed for the first pass; visual depth should be proven with terrain-owned uniforms before adding any object-level decoration.

candidates.name: ProceduralTerrains software-only style and lighting profile
candidates.source: Installed procedural-terrains@2.0.5 configuration: heightScale, style, lighting and palette controls
candidates.reason: Directly changes the shader-owned relief, tonal contrast and distance fog without adding geometry, a render pass, a dependency or a second Surface authority.

candidates.name: Existing hosted narrow Surface Playwright acceptance
candidates.source: Current mobile/tablet Surface visual cases and GitHub-hosted screenshot artifacts
candidates.reason: Provides direct before/after evidence on the software-rendered viewports that exposed the defect, with no new visual-testing system.

candidates.name: ProceduralTerrains water and cloud effect layers
candidates.reason: They can enrich a real-GPU scene but add effect preparation/render work and do not address the basic terrain tonal-depth defect on the SwiftShader tier.

candidates.name: Additional Three.js fog/light or custom atmosphere overlay
candidates.source: Three.js scene fog/lights or new product-owned atmospheric mesh
candidates.reason: The terrain shader does not use arbitrary host-scene lighting and already has its own fog control, so this would duplicate visual machinery while leaving the terrain-owned parameters underused.

decision.rationale: Tune the existing ProceduralTerrains software fallback at its own shader/configuration layer and judge the result with the already-landed hosted mobile/tablet Surface screenshots. Keep seed, octave count, Infinite World streaming, LOD budgets, lifecycle, camera authority and renderer count unchanged; promote only if visual depth improves without hosted timing or WebGL regressions.
decision.fallback: If uniform-only tuning cannot create a materially better hosted Surface composition without harming legibility or timing, keep the current profile and open a separate reuse-first candidate for one cheap package-owned atmospheric/background layer rather than broadening this task.
